title: BlackRock Bitcoin ETF Loses $2.8 Billion in Eight Consecutive Trading Sessions
summary: Key takeaways US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows in eight straight sessions from November 17 to 27, totaling about $3.44 billion. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for about $2.79 billion of that, roughly 81%. Friday’s shortened session still saw $389 million leave the funds, including $327.2 million from IBIT. IBIT’s Friday outflow was barely below Wednesday’s $329.7 million, despite the shorter trading window. ETF redemptions are not BlackRock selling its own Bitcoin, and the data does not show who is redeeming. The BlackRock Bitcoin ETF has recorded nearly $2.8 billion in net withdrawals across eight consecutive trading sessions, accounting for approximately 81% of the capital leaving US spot Bitcoin ETFs over the period. The latest figures from Farside Investors show that US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered $389 million in combined net outflows on Friday, November 27, extending a withdrawal streak that began on November 17. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $327.2 million of Friday’s withdrawals. Despite a shortened trading session following Thanksgiving, investors continued reducing their exposure through the largest Bitcoin ETF in the US. BlackRock Accounts for Most of the Bitcoin ETF Withdrawals Combined net withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs reached $3.44 billion over the eight trading sessions between November 17 and November 27. Of that amount, approximately $2.79 billion came from BlackRock’s IBIT. The fund recorded its heaviest withdrawals during this period on November 19 and 20, when investors redeemed a net $541.1 million and $544.7 million, respectively. Session IBIT All spot BTC ETFs IBIT share Nov 17 −$209.5M −$239.9M 87% Nov 18 −$148.7M −$306.5M 49% Nov 19 −$541.1M −$582.3M 93% Nov 20 −$544.7M −$669.2M 81% Nov 23 −$509.3M −$569.7M 89% Nov 24 −$175.3M −$231.4M 76% Nov 25 −$329.7M −$453.0M 73% Nov 27* −$327.2M −$389.0M 84% Total −$2.79B −$3.44B 81% Net flows of US spot Bitcoin ETFs during the eight-session withdrawal streak. *Shortened post-Thanksgiving session; US markets were closed on November 26. Data: Farside Investors. Visualization: NewsBTC. The concentration of withdrawals in IBIT is particularly important when interpreting aggregate Bitcoin ETF figures. Activity in a single fund has dominated the broader market’s recent net flows. BlackRock’s size naturally makes it more likely to account for substantial movements of capital. Its share of the outflows, therefore, should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that investors are specifically losing confidence in BlackRock. Has Bitcoin ETF Selling Actually Slowed? Friday’s $389 million in combined net outflows was lower than Wednesday’s $453 million, but the improvement was relatively modest. BlackRock’s figures were particularly revealing. IBIT recorded $327.2 million in net withdrawals on Friday, barely below the $329.7 million recorded during Wednesday’s full trading session. The shortened post-Thanksgiving trading window makes the comparison even less encouraging. CoinGlass’s historical ETF flow data also illustrates how recent withdrawals contrast with the substantial inflows recorded during earlier stages of Bitcoin’s rally. A smaller daily outflow does not necessarily signal that investors are returning. It may simply mean less capital left the funds during that particular session. What Does This Mean for Bitcoin’s Recovery? As NewsBTC previously reported, persistent withdrawals from spot Bitcoin ETFs have complicated the cryptocurrency’s attempts to establish a sustainable recovery. It is important, however, to distinguish ETF redemptions from direct selling by BlackRock itself. IBIT holds Bitcoin on behalf of its shareholders. Net withdrawals reflect activity within the fund’s creation and redemption mechanism, rather than necessarily representing a decision by BlackRock to sell Bitcoin from its own corporate balance sheet. The figures also do not reveal whether the investors behind the redemptions are institutions, financial advisers or retail participants. Monday’s trading session, the final US session of November, will offer another opportunity to assess whether demand for Bitcoin exposure is beginning to stabilize. For now, Friday’s figures provide little evidence that the withdrawal pressure has materially eased. BlackRock’s fund experienced almost the same net outflows as Wednesday, despite a shorter trading session.

title: Solana News: Developers Issue Urgent Upgrade Notice to Mainnet Validators
summary: Key takeaways Anza told Solana mainnet operators, staked and unstaked, to install Agave validator client v4.4.2 immediately. The developers said the network was continuing to operate normally; the release does not by itself indicate an outage, exploit or attack. The exact technical issue behind the urgent release has not been fully established. Validator directory data shows mixed software versions, but no verified breakdown of v4.4.2 adoption is available yet. The notice is aimed at node operators, not wallet holders, and does not by itself require SOL users to take any action. Solana developers have issued an urgent instruction to network operators, asking them to install the latest version of the Agave validator client without delay. The announcement from Anza, the development team responsible for maintaining Agave, applies to both staked and unstaked nodes running the affected software. The developers also indicated that the network was continuing to operate normally. The announcement follows a series of Solana validator software improvements introduced earlier this month, including further development of Agave and Firedancer. An urgent software update does not necessarily mean that a blockchain is experiencing an outage. In Solana’s case, the more interesting question is how quickly its distributed network of operators can respond when developers identify a problem that cannot wait for a routine upgrade. What Is Behind Solana’s Urgent Upgrade? Anza directed operators to install version 4.4.2 of its validator software, telling them in its announcement: “ Don’t wait, upgrade now. Anza · Agave v4.4.2 upgrade notice The release is documented in Anza’s official GitHub repository, while compatible builds have also reportedly been made available by Jito-Solana and Harmonic. Agave is one of the software implementations responsible for processing transactions and participating in Solana’s consensus mechanism. Validators running it help determine which transactions become part of the blockchain. Unlike updating an application on a phone, updating validator software involves coordinating machines operated by independent organizations around the world. Developers can release a new version, but the operators themselves must deploy it. Network monitoring data from Validator Info shows that both Agave 4.4.2 and Jito 4.4.2-jito have been released, while Firedancer’s latest listed version is 26.11.1. The availability of these releases does not, however, establish how many validators have installed them. That makes the speed of adoption almost as interesting as the release itself. A check of the Solana validator directory shows operators reporting different software versions, including Agave-derived implementations. However, a complete and independently verified breakdown of the latest upgrade’s adoption was not yet available. The precise technical issue behind Anza’s urgent instruction remains to be fully established. Describing the release as a response to an exploit or an active network attack would therefore be premature. Solana’s Recent Upgrades Face a Different Kind of Test The announcement comes just weeks after Solana introduced significant changes to its underlying infrastructure. As NewsBTC previously reported, the Solana Foundation introduced protocol version 1.0 in November and moved away from describing the network as mainnet beta. The distinction between the protocol version and the validator software version is important. Solana can establish a common set of network rules while individual software implementations continue to receive updates and fixes. The network has also been pursuing faster transaction processing and shorter confirmation times through its Alpenglow consensus architecture. Those improvements are valuable, but faster transactions are only useful if the infrastructure processing them remains dependable. What Does the Upgrade Mean for SOL Holders? For ordinary users, Anza’s instruction is aimed at node operators rather than wallet holders. The announcement does not, by itself, establish a need for users to move their SOL or change how they interact with the network. At the time of the dashboard snapshot, Solana had 655 active validators and five listed as delinquent. Approximately 423.44 million SOL was actively staked, representing 99.97% of the reported total stake. The figures offer a snapshot of network participation while operators are being asked to update their software, although they do not independently confirm the success of the upgrade. The next meaningful development will be evidence that operators have installed the new release and that transaction processing remains stable throughout the rollout. Solana has spent considerable time demonstrating how fast its network can become. This weekend’s upgrade offers another opportunity to assess something equally important: how well its infrastructure responds when speed is required outside of normal transaction processing.

title: Trump Crypto News: World Liberty Financial Sells $20 Million in Ethereum Assets, Data Shows
summary: Key takeaways A wallet linked to World Liberty Financial sold 10,600 WETH and 1,378 mETH for about $20.06 million. Proceeds went into about $17.58 million USDC and $2.48 million USD1, the project’s own stablecoin. On-chain analyst Ember estimates a cost of $3,244 per ETH against a disposal value near $1,655, implying a loss of about $19.26 million. The loss is an on-chain estimate, not an audited figure, and the sale covers one wallet rather than the project’s full holdings. The move reverses earlier Ethereum buying, and there is no verified evidence that Donald Trump personally directed the trades. Trump-backed crypto project World Liberty Financial has reportedly reduced its Ethereum exposure by approximately $20 million, converting two large holdings into dollar-pegged stablecoins during the latest cryptocurrency market downturn. Blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain reported that a wallet associated with the project sold 10,600 ETH and 1,378 mETH, receiving approximately $20.06 million. Separate estimates from on-chain analyst Ember suggest the assets may have been sold at a loss of more than $19 million. The transactions come just weeks after World Liberty Financial announced a WLFI token buyback program, which could be partly funded by income generated from its USD1 stablecoin reserves. The Ethereum sales represent a notable reversal for a project that previously accumulated the cryptocurrency during periods of market weakness. Where the money went, however, deserves just as much attention as what was sold. World Liberty Financial Moves Into Stablecoins The reported transactions involved approximately $17.58 million in USDC and another $2.48 million in USD1, World Liberty Financial’s own dollar-pegged stablecoin. Transaction records from Arkham show a series of transfers between World Liberty Financial’s labeled Strategic Reserve wallet and CoW Protocol, involving outgoing mETH and incoming USD1. The wallet also interacted with decentralized lending protocol Dolomite. The Ethereum assets included wrapped ether, known as WETH, and mETH, a token representing exposure to staked Ethereum. The latter distinction matters because a liquid staking token does not necessarily trade at a one-to-one ratio with ETH. Simply adding the number of WETH and mETH tokens together can give a misleading picture of the underlying Ethereum exposure. According to Ember’s estimates, the combined holdings represented approximately 12,121 ETH in equivalent exposure. The analyst estimated an average acquisition cost of $3,244 per ETH, compared with an average disposal value of approximately $1,655. If that cost-basis estimate is accurate, the transactions would represent a loss of roughly $19.26 million, or close to half the original investment. Transaction Reported figure Sold 10,600 WETH + 1,378 mETH Ethereum-equivalent exposure ≈12,121 ETH Received $17.58M USDC + $2.48M USD1 = $20.06M Estimated average cost $3,244 per ETH (≈$39.3M) Average disposal value ≈$1,655 per ETH Estimated loss ≈$19.26M (about 49%) World Liberty Financial’s reported Ethereum sale. Cost basis and loss are on-chain estimates, not audited results. Data: Lookonchain, Ember. Visualization: NewsBTC. World Liberty Financial has not been shown to have confirmed that loss in a public accounting statement. The figure remains an on-chain estimate rather than an audited financial result. Why the USD1 Transaction Matters World Liberty Financial’s decision to move part of the reported proceeds into USD1 raises questions beyond the performance of its Ethereum investments. In its official USD1 risk disclosures, World Liberty Financial acknowledges that its financial interests and those of BitGo may differ from those of USD1 holders. Both benefit from net fees earned through interest on the stablecoin’s reserves, while USD1 holders are not entitled to those earnings. That makes USD1 more than another cryptocurrency held in the project’s treasury. It is part of the business through which World Liberty Financial seeks to generate revenue from its digital-dollar product. Holding USD1, however, does not automatically generate a return for the wallet that receives it. Nor does an exchange of existing tokens necessarily increase the stablecoin’s circulating supply or reserve income. The relevant question is whether the transactions represent temporary treasury management or a broader change in the project’s investment strategy. A Reversal of Its Earlier Ethereum Strategy In January, NewsBTC reported that World Liberty Financial had acquired approximately 2,868 ETH after selling more than $8 million worth of wrapped Bitcoin. The November transactions point in the opposite direction, with the reported wallet moving away from Ethereum-linked exposure and toward dollar-denominated assets. It would nevertheless be misleading to conclude that World Liberty Financial has abandoned Ethereum entirely. The activity concerns a specific wallet, and the project’s broader holdings across other addresses have not been established by these transactions. Data from Arkham Intelligence shows that the project’s labeled Strategic Reserve wallet held approximately $243.8 million in digital assets on November 28. Notably, more than 96% of that valuation came from its own WLFI token, while the wallet retained 2,000 ETH worth approximately $3.32 million. The concentration raises a separate question about the reserve’s exposure to fluctuations in the price of its own token. Its reported portfolio value should not necessarily be confused with readily available liquidity. There is also no verified evidence that President Donald Trump personally instructed the trades. For Ethereum investors, the reported sale is another example of a large crypto-linked entity reducing exposure during a difficult market. For World Liberty Financial’s stakeholders, the more consequential questions concern its treasury strategy, the management of investment losses and the transparency of its financial disclosures. The blockchain can reveal how assets moved. It cannot, on its own, explain who authorized those movements or why.

title: Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $7.4 Billion in BTC, Breaking a Nine Year Pattern
summary: Key takeaways Balances in Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC from September 30 to November 21, worth about $7.4 billion at a reference price of $61,000. Bitcoin fell 29.5% over the same period. This group reduced its holdings in seven of the previous nine fourth quarters. Its 4.29% increase so far in Q4 2026 is the largest fourth-quarter gain since 2020. The group’s unrealized profit margin dropped from 33.9% to 5.7% by November 21, the lowest reading of 2026 in the report. Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC recorded $2.1 billion in net realized losses through November 21. Exchange inflows from transaction outputs of at least 1,000 BTC also picked up in November. Rising address balances alone cannot establish how much new money entered Bitcoin or whether its price has bottomed. Bitcoin whales have reversed their usual year-end pattern. Between September 30 and November 21, balances in addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC even though Bitcoin lost 29.5% of its value. At a reference price of $61,000, those additional coins are worth roughly $7.4 billion. The figures come from CryptoQuant’s November 27 research report, which was supported by crypto lender CoinRabbit. The study excludes exchange and mining-pool addresses from its balance cohorts. Its findings are a snapshot through November 21, not a final tally for the quarter. The timing matters. NewsBTC recently reported more than $2 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows. Fund withdrawals and rising whale balances point in different directions, but they measure different things. Neither tells us whether the same investors are moving their money from ETFs into direct Bitcoin ownership. A broader measure from Maketo’s whale holdings data puts the balance of addresses with at least 1,000 BTC at 7.22 million BTC on November 26, up 54,379 BTC over the preceding 30 days. That group includes exchange and custody addresses, so it provides a separate view of where coins are held rather than an independent check of CryptoQuant’s 121,117 BTC figure. Bitcoin Whales Reverse Their Year-End Balance Trend The combined balance of the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort at just under 2.95 million BTC on November 21, up from 2.83 million at the end of September. Large addresses reduced their balances in seven of the nine preceding fourth quarters. Only 2019 and 2020 escaped that pattern. The 4.29% increase recorded so far this quarter is the largest Q4 gain since 2020, although December could still change the result. For comparison, the cohort lost nearly 203,000 BTC over Q4 2025. This year’s increase has come during a falling market, rather than a rally. There is a catch in calling this a $7.4 billion accumulation. The figure values the additional coins at a reference price; it does not measure the dollars spent buying them. Transfers between addresses, including movements across the cohort’s balance thresholds, can change the total without a market purchase. The increase tells us where Bitcoin is sitting. It does not tell us how much fresh capital is behind it. That distinction matters when liquidity is scarce. Bitcoin Whales Are Running Out Of Profits To Protect The 121,117 BTC figure makes for a bullish headline. The number I would pay closer attention to is the remaining profit margin. Among addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC, the unrealized profit margin fell from 33.9% at the end of September to 5.7% on November 21, its lowest reading of 2026 in the report. The deterioration is even clearer in dollar terms. Combined unrealized profits for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC stood at about $24 billion on November 21, down from a peak of $294 billion in August 2025. Across the broader group of addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC, net realized losses reached approximately $2.1 billion in the first 52 days of Q4. The on-chain data suggests that some large holders are already moving coins at a loss rather than waiting for a recovery. The relevant distinction is between the balance held at a given date and the profit or loss on coins that move. A growing balance does not prevent other coins within the cohort from being spent below their estimated cost basis. Exchange deposits deserve a closer look, too. Inflows from unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) of at least 1,000 BTC averaged 5,012 BTC per day in November through the report’s cutoff, compared with 3,239 in October. That is a measure of large coin outputs, not a count of individual whales. November’s pickup should not obscure the bigger picture: the quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC per day remained below the 2019–2025 Q4 average of 4,575 BTC. Large deposits are not proof of sales, and a rise in this metric alone does not establish that selling pressure has intensified. What Would Confirm A Bitcoin Market Bottom? The 2018 and 2022 bear markets offer a useful comparison, though not a roadmap for this one. Balances in the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort declined in both of those fourth quarters. Their average unrealized profit margins were negative, while the group still had a positive margin at the November 21 reading this year. Today’s accumulation may be a sign that some large holders are willing to retain exposure through the downturn. The address data cannot establish their motives or identify how much of the increase came from new purchases. I would not call a market bottom on these numbers alone. A further price decline could wipe out the cohort’s remaining profit cushion. Whether that produces more selling depends on the holders’ liquidity needs and positioning, neither of which can be read directly from address balances. The next test is whether large-address balances keep rising while net realized losses and large exchange deposits ease. That combination, alongside evidence of renewed spot demand, would make the recovery case more convincing. For now, the change in year-end positioning is real within CryptoQuant’s measured cohort. Evidence of a durable recovery is still missing.

title: Zcash Developers Race to Secure Crypto. Can Quantum Computing Break Bitcoin?
summary: Key takeaways Zcash development team Zakura (November 26) called for accelerated retirement of the older Sapling privacy pool, which it estimated held about 400,000 ZEC. A November 27 dashboard snapshot showed about 306,684 ZEC still in Sapling, though that does not prove the warning prompted anyone to move funds. Zakura’s concern is speculative, unverified mathematical advances, not a successful quantum attack, and Shielded Labs expects to pick a post-quantum direction by the end of January 2027. The Quantum Ledger counts about 7.23 million BTC (35.9% of issued supply) with public keys already visible on-chain; Glassnode’s May estimate was 6.04 million BTC. No reliable date exists for a quantum computer that can break crypto signatures, but upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody could itself take years. Can quantum computing break crypto? For years, the question has largely been treated as a problem for the distant future. Zcash developers, however, are already discussing what to do with hundreds of thousands of coins that could become vulnerable if certain cryptographic protections fail. On November 26, Zcash development team Zakura called for the accelerated retirement of Sapling, an older privacy system that the team estimated still held around 400,000 ZEC. The recommendation followed speculation about mathematical breakthroughs at artificial intelligence laboratories. A day earlier, Shielded Labs published its first technical update on a separate project designed to protect Zcash against future quantum computers. Neither development means cryptocurrency has been cracked. Together, however, they raise a more pressing question: can blockchain developers replace the mathematics protecting investors’ money before someone finds a way around it? What Is Quantum Computing? Quantum computing is a way of processing information using the properties of quantum mechanics. Unlike conventional computers, which represent information using bits with a value of either zero or one, quantum computers operate using quantum bits, commonly known as qubits. By manipulating these qubits, researchers can design algorithms capable of solving certain mathematical problems far more efficiently than conventional computers. The important word here is certain. A quantum computer is not simply a faster version of the laptop sitting on your desk. Its advantages depend on the type of problem it is trying to solve. Unfortunately for the cryptocurrency industry, some of those problems underpin the security of digital wallets. As explained in NewsBTC’s guide to quantum computing, blockchains rely on cryptographic signatures to establish ownership and authorize transactions. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could undermine some of the signature systems currently used to protect digital assets. How Could Quantum Computers Steal Cryptocurrency? When you send Bitcoin from your wallet, the network needs to establish that you have the authority to spend those coins. It does this by verifying a digital signature produced using your private key. Your private key is supposed to remain secret. The corresponding public key can be disclosed because working backward from a public key to its private counterpart is computationally impractical using conventional methods. Quantum computing could change that. In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor introduced a quantum algorithm that could efficiently solve certain mathematical problems underlying modern public-key cryptography. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running such an algorithm could potentially recover private keys from exposed public keys. An attacker could then create a transaction that the blockchain would recognize as valid, even though the original owner had never authorized it. That is a particularly uncomfortable problem for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin does not have a customer service department that can reverse an unauthorized transfer. The National Institute of Standards and Technology has already developed alternative cryptographic standards intended to withstand these future attacks. The challenge for crypto is incorporating such protection into networks that were originally built around different assumptions. How Much Bitcoin Is Exposed to Quantum Computing? Bitcoin’s public transaction history makes it possible to estimate how much of its supply could be exposed under certain quantum attack scenarios. According to a November 25 snapshot from The Quantum Ledger, approximately 7.23 million BTC, representing 35.9% of issued supply under its methodology, was associated with public keys or spending scripts already visible on the blockchain. Around 1.94 million BTC was classified as exposed because of its output design. A further 5.29 million BTC was associated with addresses that had previously revealed relevant spending information. Some of these coins date back to Bitcoin’s earliest years, when transactions commonly revealed public keys directly. Estimates vary between researchers because they do not all measure exposure in exactly the same way. In May 2026, Glassnode’s research identified 6.04 million BTC under its own classification framework. These figures should not be interpreted as the amount of Bitcoin that will eventually be stolen. They measure a potential vulnerability under a specific future scenario, not an active attack. Owners of many exposed coins could migrate their holdings if suitable protection becomes available. Dormant wallets whose owners have lost their private keys present a considerably harder problem. Why Zcash Developers Want to Retire an Older Privacy System Zcash offers a useful example of how complicated a cryptographic migration can become. Unlike Bitcoin, where transactions are generally visible on a public ledger, Zcash provides privacy features through shielded pools. These allow users to transact without publicly revealing certain transaction details. Sapling is one of the network’s older shielded systems. Its proof mechanism relies on mathematical assumptions that Zakura believes warrant additional scrutiny in light of potentially accelerating cryptographic research. “ The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens. Zakura · Sapling retirement proposal Zakura proposed preventing new deposits into Sapling while encouraging users to migrate to Ironwood, a newer privacy system. If credible evidence of a threat emerged, further emergency measures could be considered. The amount involved is already changing. A November 27 snapshot from the Zcash Dashboard, timestamped 06:06 UTC, showed approximately 306,684 ZEC remaining in Sapling, below the rounded estimate cited in Zakura’s proposal. The difference does not, by itself, establish that the warning prompted users to move their funds. The discussion follows Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade, which improved transaction speed and continued the network’s transition away from older infrastructure. Importantly, the immediate concern raised by Zakura is not evidence of a successful quantum attack. It relates to speculative advances in mathematics that could affect particular cryptographic constructions. Those advances remain unverified. Can Zcash Become Quantum-Resistant? On November 25, Shielded Labs published an update on its Epoch project, which aims to develop privacy technology capable of withstanding future quantum computers. One of the problems its researchers are working on is the size of cryptographic proofs. Stronger protection can require considerably more data to be processed and transmitted. That can create difficulties for blockchains, where transaction capacity, verification costs and storage requirements already matter. The team is evaluating two possible approaches and expects to select a direction by the end of January 2027, provided its research progresses as planned. Ironwood already incorporates features intended to support a future recovery mechanism. However, the developers have made clear that these features do not make Zcash fully quantum-resistant today. The distinction is important. Having a contingency plan for a future attack is not the same as having protection against one. Are Bitcoin and Ethereum Preparing for Quantum Computing? Zcash is not the only network confronting these issues. Bitcoin developers are discussing changes through proposals including BIP-360, which would introduce a transaction output format designed to reduce certain forms of public-key exposure. A separate draft, BIP-361, explores a gradual transition away from vulnerable signature schemes once suitable alternatives are available. Neither proposal should be confused with an activated Bitcoin upgrade. Ethereum faces additional complications. Beyond individual wallets, its security model relies on cryptographic signatures used by validators and other infrastructure. Ethereum’s quantum-security challenge extends to staking arrangements and institutional custody. There is also a governance problem that applies particularly to Bitcoin. If millions of coins remain in old wallets that cannot be migrated, should the network eventually restrict their movement to prevent potential theft? Doing so could protect the broader ecosystem, but it could also prevent legitimate owners from accessing their own money. Leaving those coins untouched carries a different set of risks. Cryptography alone cannot settle that argument. When Will Quantum Computing Become a Real Threat to Crypto? There is no reliable date for when a quantum computer capable of breaking widely used cryptocurrency signatures will become available. Building such a machine requires more than increasing the number of qubits. Those qubits must also be reliable enough to carry out lengthy, complex calculations without errors overwhelming the results. According to Coinbase Institute’s research, the relevant machines do not yet exist, but the process of upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody infrastructure could itself take years. For that reason, waiting for an actual attack before implementing stronger cryptography would be a risky approach. Crypto investors should pay attention to what developers implement, whether wallets support the new protections and whether existing funds can be migrated without compromising ownership. There is no need to buy a token simply because its developers describe it as quantum-resistant, either. Such claims deserve scrutiny of the underlying cryptography and its implementation. Zcash’s latest proposals offer a glimpse of the decisions other blockchain communities may eventually face. Replacing an algorithm is one thing. Persuading an entire decentralized financial network to move its money before a deadline is something else entirely.

title: Ethereum’s Co-Founder Takes On Crypto’s Next Security Threat. Who Is Vitalik Buterin?
summary: Key takeaways Vitalik Buterin’s November 26 essay argues that crypto security must extend to the physical chips inside devices, summed up as “Not your silicon, not your keys.” He wants manufacturers to publish physical chip layouts (GDS files) so investigators can compare real hardware against the design. Researcher Andrew Huang’s infrared inspection technique (IRIS) can examine chips without removing them, but it has resolution limits and is not a universal fix. The essay is a proposal, not a claim that existing hardware wallets are compromised, and publishing it does not give Buterin power to change Ethereum unilaterally. Arkham attributes about $390 million in assets to Buterin, mostly roughly 224,000 ETH, though his true net worth is not publicly established. Who is Vitalik Buterin, and why is Ethereum’s co-founder now questioning the security of the very devices crypto investors use to protect their wealth? The 32-year-old programmer has turned his attention to a problem that even open-source software cannot necessarily solve: compromised computer chips. In an essay published on November 26, Buterin argued that cryptocurrency security needs to extend beyond software and into the physical hardware on which it runs. His message builds on one of crypto’s oldest principles, but with a new twist: “ Not your silicon, not your keys. Vitalik Buterin · Essay, November 26 For someone who helped build an alternative to centralized financial infrastructure, questioning the manufacturers behind that infrastructure seems like a natural next step. It also reflects a security philosophy that has become increasingly visible in Buterin’s work, from his push for greater privacy and quantum safety on Ethereum’s roadmap to his interest in independently verifiable computing. Who Is Vitalik Buterin? Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian programmer, researcher and writer who conceived Ethereum in 2013, at the age of 19. Born in Russia in 1994 and raised in Canada, Buterin discovered Bitcoin in 2011. He went on to co-found Bitcoin Magazine, where he explored the technology and economics behind cryptocurrencies long before digital assets attracted mainstream financial institutions. His involvement in Bitcoin exposed him to a problem that would eventually lead to Ethereum. Blockchain technology had potential beyond transferring money, but building more sophisticated applications on Bitcoin presented technical limitations. Rather than trying to accommodate every possible application within Bitcoin’s existing architecture, Buterin began working on a blockchain designed specifically for programmability. At the time, he was studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, where he also worked as a research assistant to cryptographer Ian Goldberg. According to the University of Waterloo, Buterin received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2014 and subsequently left university to work on Ethereum full-time. How Vitalik Buterin Created Ethereum In November 2013, Buterin wrote the initial draft of what would become the Ethereum whitepaper. The proposal described a blockchain with a general-purpose programming environment. Developers would no longer need to create an entirely new network every time they wanted to build a decentralized application. Consider a lending platform. Instead of relying on a bank to manage collateral, calculate interest and authorize withdrawals, developers could encode those rules into smart contracts running on Ethereum. That does not eliminate every risk. Smart contracts can contain bugs, depend on unreliable external data or operate under centralized administrative controls. What Ethereum introduced was the ability to execute financial and other programmable agreements on a shared blockchain. Although Buterin originated the concept, Ethereum was not built by him alone. Its founding team included seven other individuals: Gavin Wood, Joseph Lubin, Charles Hoskinson, Anthony Di Iorio, Mihai Alisie, Jeffrey Wilcke and Amir Chetrit. The project’s first live network, known as Frontier, launched on July 30, 2015. What began as an experimental computing platform eventually became the foundation for much of the decentralized finance industry. Stablecoins, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols and tokenized financial assets now use the infrastructure that Buterin and Ethereum’s early contributors helped establish. The network’s own evolution, particularly its transition to proof-of-stake and the development of Layer 2 scaling networks, has shaped Ethereum’s first decade. Vitalik Buterin’s Latest Warning: Can Crypto Wallets Really Be Trusted? A hardware wallet is supposed to keep private keys away from potentially compromised computers and smartphones. But what happens if the device itself cannot be trusted? Buterin’s latest research examines that possibility. He points to supply chain attacks involving tampered wallets and considers the potential for malicious modifications concealed inside apparently legitimate chips. Open-source firmware allows researchers to examine the instructions a device runs. But those instructions reveal little about whether the manufactured chip has been altered. Buterin wants manufacturers to disclose physical chip layouts, known as GDS files, so investigators have a reference against which to inspect actual hardware. The distinction matters. Knowing what a chip is designed to do is not necessarily the same as knowing what the chip inside your wallet actually does. The Technology That Could Help Detect Compromised Chips One approach highlighted by Buterin comes from hardware security researcher Andrew Huang, better known as bunnie. Huang has been developing a technique called Infra-Red, In Situ inspection (IRIS), which exploits the fact that silicon becomes transparent at certain infrared wavelengths. Using infrared illumination and suitable imaging equipment, researchers can examine parts of a chip’s internal structure without necessarily removing it from its circuit board. The technique could help detect substituted components or unexpected differences between manufactured chips and their intended designs. However, it is not a universal solution. In a 2024 update on his research, Huang explained that infrared imaging has resolution limits. It cannot reliably reveal every microscopic feature of modern chips. Combining imaging with additional electrical testing could improve confidence in a component’s integrity. That is an important limitation for crypto investors. Publishing an open hardware design does not automatically make a wallet secure, just as publishing a smart contract’s code does not establish that it is free of vulnerabilities. Buterin acknowledges that sophisticated hardware inspections are more likely to be performed by specialist organizations than ordinary wallet owners. His essay is a proposal for improving security, not an announcement that existing hardware wallets have all been compromised. Does Vitalik Buterin Control Ethereum? Despite his status as Ethereum’s most recognizable co-founder, Buterin is not its CEO. Ethereum is maintained through the participation of independent developers, researchers, node operators, validators and other ecosystem contributors. Changes to the network involve technical proposals, discussion, software development and adoption by participants. Buterin has considerable influence over those discussions, but publishing a proposal does not give him the authority to implement it unilaterally. His role within the Ethereum Foundation is also distinct from control over the blockchain itself. In its April 2025 governance announcement, the Foundation described Buterin’s responsibilities as providing technical and intellectual guidance to the wider ecosystem. His research can influence the direction Ethereum takes. Whether the network ultimately follows that direction depends on considerably more than his endorsement. How Much Is Vitalik Buterin Worth? Buterin accumulated considerable wealth through his involvement in Ethereum, with much of his publicly visible cryptocurrency wealth tied to ETH. However, his exact net worth is not publicly established. Blockchain analytics can estimate the value of assets held in wallets attributed to him, but those figures do not necessarily account for all his investments, liabilities, private assets or holdings at addresses that have not been publicly identified. They also fluctuate with cryptocurrency prices. A wallet valuation should therefore not be confused with a complete assessment of his personal wealth. What Is Vitalik Buterin’s Vision for the Future of Crypto? Buterin’s latest essay is part of a longer-running interest in making digital infrastructure independently verifiable. In September 2025, he published The Importance of Full-Stack Openness and Verifiability, exploring how transparency could extend across the hardware and software underpinning increasingly important parts of people’s lives. His broader research includes cryptography, privacy, blockchain scalability and Ethereum’s transition toward greater quantum resistance. Buterin has previously called for greater experimentation across Ethereum’s application layer without compromising its core principles of censorship resistance, open-source development, privacy and security. These interests share a practical concern: whether users can independently establish that the systems they rely on behave as intended. There is a commercial obstacle, though. Semiconductor manufacturers invest heavily in proprietary processes, and designing chips specifically for inspectability can involve performance compromises. But a device signing a cryptocurrency transaction does not necessarily need the computing power of a modern AI processor. That makes security-focused hardware a potentially useful starting point. More than a decade ago, Buterin challenged the idea that blockchains should primarily be used to transfer money. His latest work challenges another assumption the industry has grown comfortable with: that trusting the code is enough. For crypto investors, the next meaningful development may come from hardware manufacturers willing to make their products independently inspectable, rather than another software update promising greater security.

title: Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet
summary: Key takeaways Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes. The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales. Saylor’s personal 17,732 BTC (bought for about $175 million) would be worth roughly $1.07 billion at $60,325, assuming he still holds them all. Strategy holds 851,305 BTC bought at an average $75,446, leaving a paper shortfall of about $12.88 billion against its $64.23 billion cost. Strategy’s mNAV was 0.94 at the November 25 close, so raising capital by issuing shares has become harder, and that matters as much as the Bitcoin price. Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes. The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy. For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy. How Much Has Michael Saylor Lost During the Bitcoin Crash? Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level. His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback. Selected valuation snapshots, not daily observations. Hover over a bar for details. Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor. The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales. How Much Bitcoin Does Michael Saylor Personally Own? In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million. At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount. That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million. His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases. The situation at Strategy is quite different. Strategy Is Sitting on Nearly $13 Billion in Bitcoin Paper Losses While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations. According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC. The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446. Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26. That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings. Strategy Bitcoin portfolio Value Total holdings 851,305 BTC Average acquisition price $75,446 Total acquisition cost $64.23 billion Current Bitcoin reserve value $51.35 billion Estimated shortfall against cost $12.88 billion These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company. Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn. Why Saylor’s Fortune Is Vulnerable to More Than Bitcoin For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency. That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted. Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology. The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications: “ A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises. Strategy · Investor briefing This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test. When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition. Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements. Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin. Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much. Could Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Recover? There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound. The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations. But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model. The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders. His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

title: Monero’s Delisting Nightmare Continues: XMR Price Plunges 15%
summary: Key takeaways Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR. KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31. XMR will also stop being accepted as collateral for VIP loans, so borrowers may need to add other collateral to avoid liquidation. KuCoin is the most active XMR venue (about $62.6 million in 24-hour volume on XMR/USDT per CoinGecko), following MEXC, Binance and Kraken EEA exits. The network does not depend on KuCoin, but liquidity does: watch where volume migrates and how much slippage the remaining exchanges show. Monero (XMR) lost around 15% of its value in less than five hours on Thursday after KuCoin announced plans to remove the privacy coin from its platform. The decision comes just nine days after rival exchange MEXC discontinued XMR spot trading, leaving investors with fewer options to trade one of the cryptocurrency market’s largest privacy-focused assets. Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024. This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter. KuCoin Gives Monero Traders Four Days Before Trading Ends In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC. The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise. Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30. There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation. For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.” The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision. Monero’s Liquidity Problem Is Getting Harder To Ignore KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles. A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period. Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes. Kaiko’s historical research illustrates how liquidity across privacy cryptocurrencies had already deteriorated by early 2024, following a series of exchange restrictions. Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets. The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced. For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works. Can XMR Survive Another Major Exchange Exit? There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline. Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets. The cryptocurrency’s network does not depend on KuCoin to process transactions. Its utility as a privacy-focused payment system remains separate from its availability on centralized trading platforms. But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs. November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage. That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.
